title: Potato and Leek Soup
subtitle: Silky French classic
excerpt: A smooth, creamy soup of potato and leek with a clean, mild flavour that is as satisfying chilled in summer as it is hot in winter. Blending gives it a restaurant-quality texture with very little effort.
sourceNotes: Potato and leek soup is found across France and the British Isles, with the chilled French version known as vichyssoise credited to chef Louis Diat at the Ritz-Carlton in New York in the early twentieth century. The hot version has been a staple of Welsh and French home cooking for far longer.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the cream. Stir in cream after reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Make ahead for lunches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made a day ahead and kept in the fridge. The flavour improves overnight.

content.text: Washing leeks thoroughly is essential as grit hides between the layers. Slice them, then swish in a bowl of cold water and lift out, leaving any sand behind. Cook the leeks gently in butter until very soft before adding any liquid for the best flavour.

Melt the butter in the saucepan over a low-medium heat. Add the leek, onion, and garlic with a pinch of salt. Cook gently for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring regularly, until completely soft. Do not let them colour.
Add the diced potato and pour in the stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 18 to 20 minutes until the potato is completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Remove from the heat and ladle the soup into the blender in batches. Blend until completely smooth, being careful with the hot liquid.
Return the blended soup to the pan over a low heat. Stir in the double cream and season generously with salt and white pepper.
Ladle into warmed bowls and scatter over the chives. Add a small swirl of cream if you like.

items.symptom: Soup is gluey or starchy in texture.
items.cause: Over-blending releases too much starch from the potato.
items.fix: Blend in short pulses; stop as soon as smooth.

items.cause: The leeks were not washed thoroughly before cooking.
items.fix: Always swish sliced leeks in cold water and lift them out.

items.symptom: Soup is too thick after blending.
items.cause: Potatoes absorbed a lot of the stock during cooking.
items.fix: Stir in extra warm stock a little at a time until desired consistency.
